text.arabic_uthmani: يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ مَا لَكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِنْ عَاصِمٍۢ ۗ وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍۢ

words.gloss_range: accusative temporal frame specifying the previously warned day as a decisive event-time
words.root_gloss_range: day, time, appointed occasion, and marked event; locally narrowed to a bounded exposure-day that governs the scene
words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) does not open a loose date marker; it resumes the feared day named just before and makes this ayah specify what that day contains. The accusative temporal frame gathers the retreat, the loss of protection, and the loss of guidance into one bounded exposure-event. Its fronted position makes the listener enter the day before the fleeing addressees appear, and its compact opening releases into the longer retreat cadence before negation cuts in. Echoes such as the back-turning scene (8:16) and the no-protector pressure (11:43) remain comparative, not controlling, evidence.

topics.headline: fronted event-time resumes the warned day
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah elaborates the same feared day rather than starting a separate scene.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence both treat the word as an accusative temporal frame tied to the retreat clause, so the CRITICAL apposition and scope claims are locally licensed.

topics.headline: charged-day associations sharpen the frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the day as a disclosure-scene where retreat and rescue-denial converge, while the cited parallels remain supporting echoes.
topics.reason: The event-day sense is supported, but the cross-references to back-turning (8:16) and no-protector logic (11:43) qualify the local scene rather than governing its parse.

topics.headline: short opening releases the retreat phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the compact time-marker give way to the longer retreat phrase before negation begins.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is local and does not overrule grammar; it adds audible texture to the opening frame.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural turning away in the retreat scene, clarified by the following circumstantial participle
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, patronage, authority, turning toward, and turning away; locally narrowed to enacted withdrawal with patronage-nearness inverted

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby term or phrase referenced in the prose

words.prose: {{ar:تُوَلُّونَ}} ({{tr:tuwallūna}}) keeps the warning in direct second-person plural address: the same audience is made to inhabit the coming scene. The verb leaves the direction open until {{ar:مُدْبِرِينَ}} ({{tr:mudbirīna}}) supplies the back-facing state, so motion and posture form one retreat image. Its doubled-stem pressure makes the turn an enacted reorientation rather than a neutral change of location. The broader {{ar:و ل ي}} ({{tr:w-l-y}}) field of nearness and patronage is present as reversal: those needing protective nearness enact the root as withdrawal, a posture also comparable to the back-turning formula (8:16).

topics.headline: second-plural motion bound to the retreat state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the warned group still grammatically addressed as they turn, not merely described from a distance.
topics.reason: The verb is a 2MP imperfect, and attachment evidence binds the following participle as the ḥāl of the same subject.

topics.headline: nearness and patronage reversed into withdrawal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that a root-field associated with nearness and patronage becomes the very motion away from protection.
topics.reason: The local syntax selects turning away, while V4 supports broader nearness and patronage branches as background pressure rather than alternate local senses.

topics.headline: tightened turn before rescue denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the turn as an embodied defeat posture before the ayah removes any imagined protector.
topics.reason: The surface verb is locally tied to the back-facing participle, and the cited battlefield comparison (8:16) functions as a concrete echo.

words.gloss_range: accusative plural active participle functioning as a circumstantial state: back-facing retreaters
words.root_gloss_range: back, rear, aftermath, and management of outcomes; locally narrowed to active rearward retreat while aftermath remains a secondary pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby term or phrase referenced in the prose

words.prose: {{ar:مُدْبِرِينَ}} ({{tr:mudbirīna}}) fixes the turning as a concurrent posture: they turn while already marked as back-facing retreaters. The plural participle distributes that exposed posture across the addressed group, and its root-field lets the body image carry an aftermath pressure: their backs face away while the consequence follows. The defeat vocabulary echo, including the turning-backs scene (54:45), remains a supporting comparison for the local motion-posture pair, and the long-vowel retreat phrase stretches before {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) cuts into negation.

topics.headline: circumstantial back-facing posture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first beat as a full posture scene, not simply a verb of motion.
topics.reason: The word is a masculine plural accusative active participle and attachment evidence makes it the ḥāl of the addressed subject.

topics.headline: back-side image with aftermath pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that rearward bodily exposure and unmanageable consequence converge in the selected root field.
topics.reason: The local ḥāl selects retreat, while the broader root range supports aftermath and management only as qualified background pressure.

topics.headline: retreat vocabulary lands the beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees the retreat phrase land before the negated protection clause begins.
topics.reason: The same adjacent motion-posture pair is locally present, and the cited defeat comparison (54:45) supports the retreat texture without overriding the ayah's judgment-day setting.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening a negated existential possession clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby term or phrase referenced in the prose

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) changes the ayah from movement to absence. It opens a verbless negative existential frame, so the issue is not a failed rescue attempt but the non-availability of any protector at all. As the first standalone negative particle, it also sets the template that later returns in {{ar:فَمَا}} ({{tr:fa-mā}}), making loss of protection and loss of guidance formally parallel.

topics.headline: no-protector clause begins as existence-denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that protection is removed at the level of availability, before any rescuer can act.
topics.reason: The clause is identified as a negated existential nominal clause, and the following extra-min construction confirms exhaustive absence.

topics.headline: first negative template anticipates the second
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first denial prepare the later no-guide denial as a matched structure.
topics.reason: The repeated negative architecture is visible across the two clauses, with the second occurrence linked by the conditional answer.

words.gloss_range: fronted prepositional predicate assigning availability to the directly addressed plural group

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby term or phrase referenced in the prose

words.prose: {{ar:لَكُم}} ({{tr:lakum}}) makes the denial personal and communal: the question is what stands available for you, the addressed group, not whether protectors exist somewhere in abstraction. The lām frames possession, benefit, or allocation, and the negation removes those routes specifically from the fleeing addressees. This plural frame later becomes {{ar:لَهُ}} ({{tr:lahu}}), shifting the same no-availability syntax from the direct audience to an individual conditional case.

topics.headline: availability denied on the addressees' side
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the loss is allocated to the warned audience, not stated as an abstract fact about protection.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the prepositional phrase as the fronted predicate in the negated possession clause.

topics.headline: plural warning prepares singular rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah will preserve the same possession template while moving from a group warning to a one-person rule.
topics.reason: The later matching prepositional predicate is syntactically parallel, so the plural-to-singular movement is visible in the local structure.

words.gloss_range: preposition before the divine name, allowing source and separation/against relations in the no-protector frame
words.prose: {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) places the absent protector in relation to God before the protector is even named. The preposition can mark source or separation, so the local phrase allows both pressures: no protection sourced from God is available, and no separation from God's judgment can be achieved. The vowel is a liaison before the divine name, preserving the same preposition while making the dependency pronounceable.

topics.headline: source and separation pressure before the protector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the protector problem is measured through relation to God before any candidate protector is considered.
topics.reason: The phrase governs the divine name in the no-protector clause; source and separation are both possible prepositional pressures, but neither should be made exclusive.

topics.headline: vowelled form carries the relation into the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can register that the written/sounded form joins the preposition smoothly to the following divine name without creating a new particle.
topics.reason: The surface vowel is phonological liaison before the divine name and does not alter the preposition's syntactic role.

words.gloss_range: genitive proper divine name governed by the preceding preposition in the no-protector clause
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with derivational discussions around worship, refuge, and bewilderment; locally the proper name fixes the unique divine relation controlling rescue

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby term or phrase referenced in the prose

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:llāhi}}) anchors the first denial in relation to the named God, not to an abstract force. Its genitive case after {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) means the missing protector is measured by divine relation before the noun {{ar:عَاصِمٍ}} ({{tr:ʿāṣimin}}) appears. The derivational pressure around worship, refuge, and bewilderment is useful background, but the local payoff is sharper: no protector can be detached from the unique divine referent, and the same name later returns as nominative agent.

topics.headline: named divine relation controls possible rescue
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that rescue is evaluated in relation to the named God before any protector category is denied.
topics.reason: The proper noun is genitive after the preposition and is attached inside the no-protector clause.

topics.headline: worship and refuge background remains bounded
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a refuge-seeking background that fits the no-protector scene without replacing the proper-name function.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute is meaningful as pressure around the divine name, but local grammar keeps the word functioning as the proper divine name.

topics.headline: genitive name prepares nominative reprise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same divine name move from relation in the protection clause to agency in the misguidance clause.
topics.reason: Both occurrences of the proper name are aligned in the ayah with distinct case roles, supporting the structural echo.

words.gloss_range: extra/minimality marker before an indefinite participle under negation, exhausting the protector class

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby term or phrase referenced in the prose

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) before the indefinite protector turns the negative clause into exhaustive denial: not even one candidate from the protector class remains. Its bare form contrasts with the preceding {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}), so the phrase moves from divine relation to a failed search for any protector.

topics.headline: not even one protector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar denies the minimal possible protector, not just a known protector.
topics.reason: The particle precedes an indefinite participle inside a negated existential clause, matching the exhaustive/minimality construction.

topics.headline: second preposition closes the layered phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the two nearby prepositions doing different jobs: relation to God, then exhaustive absence of a candidate.
topics.reason: The first prepositional phrase governs the divine name, while this one governs the indefinite protector.

words.gloss_range: indefinite active participle: any acting protector or restraining rescuer, negated under exhaustive min
words.root_gloss_range: protecting, preserving, holding back, restraining, and holding fast; locally an active protector/restrainer is denied as a class

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby term or phrase referenced in the prose

words.prose: {{ar:عَاصِمٍۢ}} ({{tr:ʿāṣimin}}) is the absent agent on which the first denial lands. Because it is singular, indefinite, active, and governed by {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) under negation, the clause erases even one capable protector rather than one known rescuer. The {{ar:ع ص م}} ({{tr:ʿ-ṣ-m}}) field adds shielding and restraining force: the missing agent would have to protect them and hold the exposure back. The no-protector echo from (11:43) supports this as a marked active-rescue denial, later mirrored by the absent guide.

topics.headline: whole protector class erased
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the verse denies any acting rescuer at all, not merely the failure of a familiar helper.
topics.reason: The active participle is indefinite after exhaustive {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) in a negated existential clause.

topics.headline: shielding and restraint both fail
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the absent protector would need to shield and restrain, so rescue fails both as cover and as prevention.
topics.reason: The root range supports protect/hold-back pressure, while local grammar selects the active protector noun rather than self-restraint as the direct sense.

topics.headline: protector prepares the absent guide
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first missing agent, protector, set up the second missing agent, guide, through the same indefinite participle grammar.
topics.reason: The pair of indefinite active participles under {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) is locally visible, and the no-protector comparison (11:43) supports the rescue-denial formula.

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) prevents the second half from floating away as an unrelated maxim. It adds and resumes: the no-guide condition is joined to the no-protector warning while restarting the syntax with {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}). The written bundle {{ar:وَمَنْ}} ({{tr:wa-man}}) makes the universal rule visibly attached to the preceding scene.

topics.headline: conditional rule stays attached to the warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the theological rule explain the warning rather than replace it with a disconnected statement.
topics.reason: The conjunction opens the conditional segment immediately after the no-protector clause, so addition and resumption both fit the local discourse.

topics.headline: direct warning becomes a general rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from a plural addressed audience to a rule applying beyond that audience.
topics.reason: The conjunction is analytically split but orthographically bundled with the conditional head, visibly tying the universalization to the preceding warning.

words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the conditional rule by placing the affected person first. It is not only a condition marker; attachment evidence makes it the fronted object of {{ar:يُضْلِلِ}} ({{tr:yuḍlili}}), so the person misled is heard before the divine action and subject are named. Its open personal scope is later resumed by the singular pronoun in {{ar:لَهُ}} ({{tr:lahu}}), individualizing the rule without narrowing it.

topics.headline: affected person placed before the action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the misled person foregrounded before the verb and divine subject appear.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence explicitly marks the conditional head as the fronted object of the misguidance verb.

topics.headline: whoever opens the rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from a direct plural warning to a universal personal case.
topics.reason: The later singular pronoun resumes the conditional head, preserving open scope while applying it to each case.

words.gloss_range: causative misguidance verb in the conditional protasis, with the affected object fronted and the divine subject following
words.root_gloss_range: wandering, losing the road, error, and being astray; locally causative misdirection that creates the no-guide result

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby term or phrase referenced in the prose

words.prose: {{ar:يُضْلِلِ}} ({{tr:yuḍlili}}) supplies the condition that the final denial answers. Its causative Form IV makes the issue more than a person wandering and differs from an intensive repeated-misleading profile; the named subject governs a decisive derouting, and the apodosis denies the guide who could reverse it. The root-field of road-loss and moral error is selected because {{ar:هَادٍ}} ({{tr:hādin}}) is withheld as the exact counter-agent. The same divine-action root is picked up again in the next ayah (40:34), where the rule becomes diagnosis.

topics.headline: causative protasis governs the result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the no-guide clause is the required answer to a governed condition, not an independent aside.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the verb as the conditional protasis whose apodosis is marked by the following result particle.

topics.headline: the problem names the remedy it removes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb creates precisely the need that the final guide-word denies.
topics.reason: The root-pair with guidance is locally active because the verb is followed by the negated active guide; the comparison to the paired language at (2:26) supports the antithesis.

topics.headline: decisive causation, not iterative misdirection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the chosen form as a conditional divine derouting that is immediately reprised in the next ayah (40:34).
topics.reason: The form-specific contrast is valid as a narrowing: the local verb is causative in the conditional frame, while intensive or repeated misleading remains a nonlocal contrast.

words.gloss_range: nominative proper divine name as explicit postverbal subject of the misguidance verb
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with worship/refuge derivational pressure; locally the named God is the explicit agent in the conditional clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:llāhu}}) is retained as the explicit nominative subject after the misguidance verb, so the condition is not an impersonal drift into error. The verb is heard first and then assigned to the named God, which delays the agent without hiding agency. This second occurrence also changes the earlier genitive divine relation into nominative action: the ayah moves from no protector in relation to God to no guide when God is the acting subject. The close no-guide formula (7:186) is therefore embedded after a concrete retreat scene, not left as an abstract maxim.

topics.headline: named subject blocks impersonal misguidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees misguidance assigned to the named divine subject, not to a vague process.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the proper name as the explicit subject of the verb.

topics.headline: relation becomes agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated name changes case and role, tightening the ayah from divine relation to divine action.
topics.reason: The same proper name appears as genitive in the first half and nominative subject here.

topics.headline: formulaic no-guide logic after the flight scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the close no-guide formula (7:186) embedded after the concrete retreat scene rather than floating as a detached maxim.
topics.reason: The recurrence supports a formulaic connection, but the local verse still controls the exact syntax and narrative placement.

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) binds the no-guide clause to the condition before it. Unlike the looser continuation of {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}), this particle supplies consequence: if God misguides someone, then no guide is available for him. Because it is fused to the following negator in {{ar:فَمَا}} ({{tr:fa-mā}}), the result relation and denial arrive as one surface movement.

topics.headline: no-guide is the required result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees guide-absence as the consequence required by the condition, not a separate observation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following clause as the answer to the conditional protasis.

topics.headline: continuation tightens into consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse tighten from added rule to logically bound result.
topics.reason: The local sequence uses conjunction before the conditional head and result particle before the apodosis.

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) keeps its negating force inside {{ar:فَمَا}} ({{tr:fa-mā}}). It scopes over {{ar:لَهُ مِنْ هَادٍ}} ({{tr:lahu min hādin}}), so the result clause states immediate non-availability of a guide rather than narrating guidance failing over time. By repeating the earlier negative architecture, it makes the no-guide clause formally answer the no-protector clause.

topics.headline: guide availability is denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the apodosis as immediate absence of any guide for the conditioned person.
topics.reason: The particle negates the possession predicate in the conditional result clause.

topics.headline: second negation mirrors the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that loss of guidance repeats the syntax of loss of protection.
topics.reason: The second negative clause shares the same prepositional possession and exhaustive-min architecture.

words.prose: {{ar:لَهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) carries the conditional person into the result clause. The attached singular pronoun resumes {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), so an open whoever-rule becomes a concrete individual case without losing its universal scope. At the same time, the phrase mirrors {{ar:لَكُم}} ({{tr:lakum}}): the ayah keeps the no-availability syntax but moves from the addressed group to the misled individual.

topics.headline: the whoever becomes him
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the universal condition applied to each individual misled person.
topics.reason: The pronoun in the prepositional predicate resumes the conditional head and governs the no-guide availability frame.

topics.headline: plural warning narrows to one case
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same denial template move from the community addressed to the singular person governed by the rule.
topics.reason: The two prepositional predicates are syntactically parallel while differing in person and number.

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) before {{ar:هَادٍ}} ({{tr:hādin}}) repeats the exhaustive marker used before the absent protector. Under negation it empties the guide class down to zero: not even one guide remains available. Its unfused shape isolates the final denial and makes no-guide answer no-protector structurally.

topics.headline: not even one guide
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the clause denies the whole class of possible guides, not just a preferred guide.
topics.reason: The particle precedes an indefinite active participle in a negated result clause.

topics.headline: same particle slot repeats the denial pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices no-guide as the second instance of the same min-plus-indefinite-participle denial pattern.
topics.reason: The same construction occurs before both absent agents in the ayah.

words.prose: {{ar:هَادٍۢ}} ({{tr:hādin}}) is the ayah's final absent agent. As an indefinite active participle after {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) under negation, it denies any acting guide, not merely an abstract route or one known helper, and it mirrors {{ar:عَاصِمٍ}} ({{tr:ʿāṣimin}}) as a second min-governed absent agent. The {{ar:ه د ي}} ({{tr:h-d-y}}) field is the direct remedy for {{ar:ض ل ل}} ({{tr:ḍ-l-l}}), so the verse names guidance only to remove the agent who could supply it. Its closure gathers several pressures: the no-guide formula (39:36), the earlier guidance claim reversed in this surah (40:29), the immediate diagnostic reprise (40:34), and the recitational variant that changes final duration without changing the no-guide syntax.

topics.headline: any acting guide is unavailable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the result clause deny a personal directing agent, not only guidance as content.
topics.reason: The word is an indefinite active participle after exhaustive {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) in a negated apodosis.

topics.headline: the remedy to misguidance is named and removed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word is the exact counter-root remedy to misguidance, made unavailable.
topics.reason: The local pairing of the misguidance verb and the denied guide activates the problem/remedy antithesis, with the formula comparison (39:36) supporting the result.

topics.headline: semantic closure with recitational pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verse closing on denied guidance, with the variant affecting sound and pause rather than the grammar of absence.
topics.reason: The variant pressure concerns final sound/duration; local syntax remains the min-governed indefinite no-guide construction.

topics.headline: final guide-word ties the ayah and surah together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final word echo the absent protector inside the ayah and prepare the next ayah's repeated misguidance diagnosis (40:34).
topics.reason: The final guide noun mirrors the earlier absent protector and connects to concrete same-surah references (40:29 and 40:34) without changing the local apodosis.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ ... مِنْ عَاصِمٍ ... مِنْ هَادٍ
baseline_models.mechanism: A severe event becomes a rout: doubled back-turning removes both protection from harm and orientation toward a viable direction.

activation_trace.role: The branch's severe event gives the temporal frame the pressure of a crisis rather than a neutral date.
Turning away supplies the first act of retreat and relational disengagement.
Presenting the back in flight intensifies the retreat into exposed rout.
Preventive holding and preservation supplies the protection explicitly absent.
Deviation from intended direction explains why movement does not become escape.
Gentle indication toward a true road supplies the orienting function explicitly absent.

changed_reading.before: The ayah says that people flee on judgment day and have no savior or guide.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages an exposed rout in which rapid movement, loss of protection, and loss of direction form one failed-escape mechanism.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ followed by the negated عَاصِم and هَاد
baseline_models.mechanism: The same focus root that can image proximity, guardianship, and support is realized as turning away; the doubled retreat therefore reads as a reversal of sustaining relation, not locomotion alone.

activation_trace.role: Nearness without an interval supplies the relational state that the enacted turning reverses.
Alliance and support make the lost proximity specifically protective rather than merely spatial.
The actual verbal branch selects withdrawal and rejection from among those relational possibilities.
Mutual back-turning and estrangement extends the bodily posture into severed social relation.
Protective holding names the relational function no longer available after the reversal.

changed_reading.before: Turning the back is simply the visible posture of fugitives.
changed_reading.after: Turning the back enacts a reversal from proximity and protective alliance into estrangement, after which neither holding protection nor orientation remains.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah places formally parallel claims to guide toward the path of right in Pharaoh's mouth and the believer's mouth, while divine guidance and misguidance bracket them. The focus clause therefore adjudicates effective guidance: a claimed guide can name a path yet cannot make it traversable when divine misguidance has taken effect.

activation_trace.role: Guidance as indication toward road and truth is the efficacy denied to every would-be guide.
The prior divine negation makes guidance depend on more than a human claim to know a road.
Pharaoh appropriates the language of indicating a true road for his own asserted leadership.
The extended walkable road gives Pharaoh's claim a concrete route rather than abstract advice.
Straight guidance away from error is the destination Pharaoh claims for his route.
The repeated causative misguidance immediately after the focus confirms that deviation can defeat asserted direction.
The believer repeats the same guiding function but couples it to following rather than coercive assertion.
The same walkable-road image makes the two rival claims formally comparable.
Right direction names the shared claimed endpoint while leaving the claims' efficacy unequal.

structural_cues: 40:29 and 40:38 repeat أَهْدِيكُمْ سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ with different speakers on opposite sides of the focus.
40:28 negates divine guidance for a prodigal liar, and 40:34 repeats the focus's divine causative misguidance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies paired human guide claims plus divine guidance and misguidance; I infer that 40:33 revokes the performative efficacy of rival guide claims, while the live alternative is that it states a general maxim without adjudicating those speeches.

changed_reading.before: No guide means that nobody will offer correct directions.
changed_reading.after: Many voices can still claim the path of right, but no claimant can convert speech into an effective road for one whom God has caused to stray.

context_deltas.mechanism: A near-verbal echo denies any warder against God, yet refuge in God and entrusting the affair to God are followed by God's protection. The negation is directional rather than an absolute denial of protection: no independent shield can interpose against God, while protection can occur by reorientation into God's keeping.

activation_trace.role: Protective holding is the focus function whose source and direction the context clarifies.
The warding of harm appears in a close negated echo: no warder from or against God.
Seeking refuge and protective attachment supplies the positive orientation into divine shelter.
Aid that makes its recipient prevail sharpens the question of who could help against God's force.
Returning one's affair to another in reliance supplies the relational act preceding protection.
God's actual warding of harm shows that the surah does not deny protection in every relation.

structural_cues: 40:21 ما كان لهم من الله من واق closely anticipates 40:33 ما لكم من الله من عاصم.
The sequence 40:44-45 moves directly from entrusting the affair to God to God's protection from plotted harms.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the negated warder, refuge, entrustment, and subsequent protection; I infer that مِنَ اللَّهِ is oriented against divine action and that safety is available only within divine keeping, while the live alternative reads it simply as source and keeps the protected believer as a different case.

changed_reading.before: The ayah declares an absolute absence of any protector.
changed_reading.after: The ayah denies an autonomous shield against God; its sharper contrast is between futile protection from God and effective refuge in God's keeping.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding 'day of calling' makes the focus day acoustic and public. Its next action is back-turning, and later calls are characterized as lost, so the rout becomes a collapse of addressability: calls circulate, but no answering guide can orient the fugitives.

activation_trace.role: The severe-event day receives its acoustic and public specification from the preceding calling.
Turning away becomes the failed response made to the surrounding calls.
Raised voice and calling make the day an active field of summons rather than silent panic.
The gathering-place branch adds a public social field in which the calls and retreat are exposed.
Calling that seeks to incline an addressee supplies the response-demand whose efficacy later fails.
Loss gives the disbelievers' call the status of an address that cannot reach an effective destination.

structural_cues: 40:32 يَوْمَ التَّنَادِ is followed immediately by 40:33 يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ, allowing the second day-clause to elaborate the first.
The repeated مِنْ negations leave both protective and guiding response roles unoccupied.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency between the day of calling and the day of retreat plus a later lost call; I infer a call-response mechanism, while the live alternative treats the two day-clauses as parallel descriptions and the later prayer as a separate scene.

changed_reading.before: The fugitives run in a chaotic but otherwise silent scene.
changed_reading.after: They turn away inside a public field of summons whose calls no longer secure either an answering protector or an orienting guide.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated causative misguidance is attached to exceeding limits and agitated doubt, then followed by sealing and being barred from the road. Misguidance thus reads as a stabilized feedback loop: prior excess and doubt are stamped into a disposition that reproduces further turning away.

activation_trace.role: Deviation from intended direction is the focus condition to be explained as process rather than label.
Immediate repetition keeps divine causative deviation active across the focus boundary.
Exceeding the limit supplies a prior trajectory that misguidance can stabilize.
Agitated doubt supplies the unstable cognition that becomes locked rather than resolved.
Stamping and sealing supplies the mechanism by which a repeated trajectory becomes fixed.
Diversion and turning away externalize the sealed disposition as blocked movement.
The walkable road supplies the route from which the subject is barred.

structural_cues: 40:34-37 sequences causative misguidance, prodigality and doubt, sealing, beautified action, and diversion from the path.
The focus's causative يُضْلِلِ and the later passive صُدَّ leave different grammatical views of the same blocked trajectory.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the sequence and repeated turning vocabulary; I infer the arrow excess and doubt -> sealing -> self-reproducing diversion, while the live alternative takes sealing as a verdict on an already complete condition rather than its sustaining mechanism.

changed_reading.before: God's misguidance is a one-time displacement onto the wrong road.
changed_reading.after: Misguidance is a feedback lock in which exceeded limits and unresolved doubt become sealed into a disposition that keeps turning from the available road.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah distinguishes a sought way out and an offered salvation from mere retreat, then places all subjects inside return to God and a fixed abode. Back-turning is therefore abundant motion without an exit: a real escape had the form of accepting the offered route, whereas fugitive motion after refusal remains enclosed by return.

activation_trace.role: Retreat supplies motion away from the immediate scene but not yet a destination outside it.
The end and outcome branch makes the direction of flight answerable to its eventual terminus.
Passing outside supplies the explicit but unanswered desire for an exit.
A traversable road turns the desired exit into a route problem.
Fixity and settlement give the afterlife abode the stable endpoint that flight cannot dissolve.
Salvation as separation supplies the real exit offered before the scene of failed flight.
Return to a place closes the imagined outside into which fugitives might flee.
Being brought back confirms return as the terminal direction of apparently outward motion.

structural_cues: 40:11 explicitly asks whether there is any path of exit, while 40:41 offers salvation as a competing destination.
40:43 and 40:77 repeat return to God after the focus's imagery of turning away.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exit, salvation, settlement, and return language; I infer a closed movement topology in which rejected salvation converts later flight into return, while the live alternative keeps these as separate eschatological statements without a shared spatial mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Turning their backs is movement away and therefore at least an attempted escape.
changed_reading.after: Their retreat is motion inside a closed return: the offered escape was a prior reorientation, and back-turning after its refusal has no outside endpoint.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the material strap branch of ع ص م rather than only its dominant protective sense. It remains anchored in the focus noun عَاصِم and gains packet support from the later collar, linked chain, neck, and dragging sequence. Downstream prose should present it as a material analogy that sharpens failed protection, not as a replacement lexical translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: عَاصِمٍ as both protective holding and, through its branch inventory, a strap or handhold

activation_trace.role: A strap, rope, or prepared handhold materializes the absent means of protective attachment.
A collar that binds an organ supplies the punitive inverse of a safety attachment.
The neck locates the imposed attachment on the fleeing body.
Connected links turn attachment from a possible handhold into continuous restraint.
Dragging and extension convert self-directed flight into externally imposed transport.

changed_reading.before: There is no savior able to stop the punishment.
changed_reading.after: There is no protective tether to grasp; the only later attachment is its punitive inverse, a collar-and-chain system that drags the former fugitives.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates هَاد as a leader or vanguard and places that image against the salient backs of مُدْبِرِينَ. It remains directly anchored in two focus words and produces a coherent spatial mechanism. Downstream prose should qualify it as a secondary spatial overlay on moral guidance, not as the primary sense of هَاد.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: مُدْبِرِينَ paired with the negated هَاد

activation_trace.role: The visible backs establish the rearward pole of the fleeing formation.
A guide who advances at the front supplies the missing forward pole and leading line.

changed_reading.before: The fugitives lack someone who can tell them where to go.
changed_reading.after: The rout is spatially frontless: backs are everywhere, but no vanguard occupies the forward position that could turn a crowd into an oriented formation.

strongest_changes: The negated protector becomes directional: no shield can interpose against God, although protection in God's keeping remains live.
The negated guide adjudicates rival claims to the same path of right, distinguishing named routes from divinely effective guidance.
The day of calling, failed calls, sealed diversion, and final return turn flight into a collapse of response and route rather than locomotion alone.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet exposed a close no-warder echo, mirrored human guide claims, and a movement sequence from public calling and back-turning through blocked roads to return and forced dragging; these supported several coexisting changes without reducing the focus to one theme.
remaining_uncertainties: The directional reading of مِنَ اللَّهِ remains syntactically live beside a source reading.
The arrow from excess and doubt through sealing to repeated diversion is reader-supplied from sequence, not explicitly stated as a causal chain.
The tether and front-of-formation readings are branch-backed analogies and should remain secondary to the dominant protection and guidance senses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Turning the back spatializes failed escape.** `د ب ر/B001` supplies the rear of a thing, while `ع ص م/B001` supplies a restraining hold that protects and is negated. I infer flight directed away from judgment but lacking any protective grip. “Retreating” reads as exposed rearward motion, not strategic withdrawal.
2. **Direction and protection fail together.** `ض ل ل/B001` is deviation from aim; `ه د ي/B001` is guidance toward a way. Their causal opposition follows the absent protector. I infer that no route can function when the orienting relation itself is lost; the ayah joins spatial escape and moral direction in one failed navigation.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The dragging chains of 40:71 retrospectively reverse the flight image: unprotected self-motion ends as compelled rearless movement.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Backward flight lacks both a hold and a heading.** Lexically, `د ب ر:B003` is "turning the back and withdrawing," `ع ص م:B001` a "restraining hold that protects," and `ه د ي:B002` an intended direction. Structurally, the mutual calling of 40:32 gives way to backs turned; neither protective restraint nor guide remains, and 40:34 then shows a long history of unsettled direction. The hold would arrest outward flight and guidance would orient it, but both are negated. The packet supplies posture and absences; I infer that misdirection manifests bodily as withdrawal no attachment can stop. The ayah reads as a complete failure of navigation, not merely as running plus two independent theological statements.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 40:69-71 turns directional failure into passive diversion and dragging, revealing backward flight as an early bodily form of transferred control over movement.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P2 Coercive Force and Protective Holding
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Political force attempts to seize and destroy, while refuge works by holding the threatened subject out of that force's reach.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Refuge is rendered as a retaining rope, barrier, or protective binding that counters coercive control.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Refuge as Restraint against Seizure
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: The threatened speaker seeks a protector who can interpose a barrier, retain him securely, and vindicate him against attack.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: refuge `quranic:root_001059:B001/m01`; protective amulet `quranic:root_001059:B002/m01`; escape from threatened killing `quranic:root_001059:B006/m01`; holding or preventing seizure `quranic:root_001021:B001/m01`; retaining rope or strap `quranic:root_001021:B002/m01`; protective barrier `quranic:root_001677:B001/m01`; vindicating aid `quranic:root_001510:B002/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Refuge is not simple withdrawal. It is a counter-grip: a protective holder prevents hostile seizure and preserves the speaker long enough for vindication.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Hem doğal gündüz sınırının hem de bunun tek bir sayılabilir birim olduğunun açıkça belirtilmesi gereken bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Sınırlandırılmış gündüz süresini ve onun tek bir gün birimi oluşunu birlikte korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyük olay, olayın gerçekleşmesi, şiddetli gün ve çoğulda yaşanmış olaylar kullanımlarını aynı dalda toplar. Bu çerçeve kullanılabilir, ancak bunların tek bir yalın anlam değil, gün ile olay arasındaki aktarmaya dayanan bağlı kullanımlar olduğu açıkça belirtilmelidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, büyük veya çetin olayla bağlantılı mecazî ve kalıplaşmış kullanımlarla sınırlıdır; literal zaman süresi ve yalnızca Tanrı'ya bağlanan anma günleri dışarıda kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Olayı anlatan biçimsel genişleme, şiddetli gün bildiren kalıplar ve çoğul olay anlamı ayrı yüzler olarak korunur; kalıp anlamları yalın kullanıma genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Büyük veya çetin bir olayın gerçekleştiği kritik günü ya da olayın kendisini anlatan aktarmalı kullanımdır. Bazı kalıplarda çok ağır bir gün, çoğul biçimde ise yaşanmış önemli olaylar anlamı taşır.

facets.statement: Gün sözü, büyük bir olay gerçekleştiğinde o kritik zamanı veya gerçekleşen olayı anlatmak üzere aktarılır.
Belirli kalıplarda günün çok çetin, ağır ve etkisi uzun süren bir gün olduğu vurgulanır.
Çoğul biçim, bilinen günlerde gerçekleşmiş önemli olayları veya tarihî vakaları anlatabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar gün sözünün büyük bir olayın gerçekleşmesine aktarılmasını, çetin gün anlatımında kullanılmasını ve çoğul biçimin olayları belirtmesini aynı anlamsal aile içinde verir.
